source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text for all four arXiv papers. Casimir 1948 and Brown-Maclay 1969 are NAMED-NOT-READ; their formulas are taken from the review's eqs (2.36)-(2.37), (4.31) and Sopova-Ford eq (52), and Mostepanenko 2021 eqs (1)-(2), which agree with each other.

published_statement: As restated (quant-ph/0106045 p.25 eqs 2.36-2.37): for two perfectly conducting parallel plates of area S -> oo at separation a, the renormalised vacuum energy (Minkowski contribution in the gap subtracted) is E0ren(a) = -(c hbar pi^2/(720 a^3)) S and the force F(a) = -dE/da = -(pi^2/240)(hbar c/a^4) S. Mostepanenko 2021 p.1-2: 'two parallel, electrically neutral ideal metal plates at zero temperature spaced in vacuum at a distance a attract each other ... F_IM(a) = -pi^2 hbar c/(240 a^4) ... E_IM(a) = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 a^3). This is the Casimir energy per unit area of the plates.' The LOCAL energy density is not Casimir's 1948 statement but Brown-Maclay 1969, restated in Sopova-Ford p.1: 'Brown and Maclay showed that for perfectly conducting plates, one has a constant negative vacuum energy density', and eq (52): 'In the limit omega_p -> oo ... we get the familiar result U = -pi^2/(720 a^4)' (hbar = c = 1).
published_hypotheses: perfect (ideal) conductors: E_t|S = H_n|S = 0 on both plates, i.e. reflection of every frequency (review p.23 eq 2.27; p.154: 'The original Casimir result (1.3) is valid only for perfect conductors of infinitely high conductivity ... for sufficiently high frequency any metal becomes transparent')
infinite plane-parallel plates, S -> oo (review eq 2.29)
zero temperature (Mostepanenko 2021 p.1; review p.79: thermal effect 'negligible for a << hbar c/(k_B T)')
free quantised electromagnetic field in the gap, two polarisations; energy renormalised by subtracting the Minkowski vacuum in the same volume (review eq 2.33)

for the LOCAL density (Brown-Maclay via Sopova-Ford): perfect conductivity again; with a dispersive (plasma-model) wall the density acquires a positive position-dependent term, diverges at the interface, and is negative at the midpoint only for omega_p a > ~99 (Sopova-Ford eqs 50-51, p.13: 'a > a_c = 99/omega_p = 1.3 um (14.8 eV/omega_p)')

validity of the ideal limit for real metals requires a >> lambda_p (review p.155-156: plasma-model perturbation in delta0/a works for a >= lambda_p); below a few nm the Casimir force IS the non-retarded van der Waals force (Mostepanenko 2021 p.2; review eq 4.27, F = -H/(6 pi a^3))

later_literature.ref: quant-ph/0204125 Sopova & Ford 2002, 'The Energy Density in the Casimir Effect'
later_literature.what: With dispersive (plasma-model) walls the gap energy density = negative constant (Casimir) term + positive position-dependent term diverging at the interface; midpoint negative only for omega_p a > ~99 (a > 1.3 um for 14.8 eV); recovers -pi^2/(720 a^4) as omega_p -> oo. 'The existence of an attractive Casimir force is not an indicator of whether the energy density at the center of the plates is actually negative or not.' Reproduced numerically here.

Only parallel-plate measurement read: force coefficient K_C = (1.22 +- 0.18)e-27 N m^2 over 0.5-3.0 um, 15% precision, agreeing with Casimir's pi h c/480; fitted exponent 5.0 +- 0.1 for the dynamic signal (d^-4 force).

later_literature.ref: quant-ph/0106045 Bordag, Mohideen, Mostepanenko 2001, Phys. Rep. 353, 1
later_literature.what: Casimir's result 'valid only for perfect conductors'; finite-conductivity corrections 10-20% at ~1 um (eq 5.60, valid for a >= lambda_p); non-retarded van der Waals limit F = -H/(6 pi a^3) for a << lambda_0 (eq 4.27); thermal corrections large beyond a few um (86-174% at 4-6 um).

Real-metal Lifshitz theory with the Drude model is excluded by precision data (160-750 nm Au, 223-420 nm Ni, differential up to x1000) while the plasma model agrees; Nernst-theorem problems; unresolved. Concerns the few-percent real-material/thermal corrections at 0.2-1 um, not the ideal limit; also states the Casimir force becomes the non-retarded van der Waals force below a few nm. Does not move the tree's conclusions (plasma model was used here; Drude would reduce the force further at finite T).

lacked_data: What Casimir (1948) lacked: any measurement (first attempt Sparnaay 1958, 'do not contradict'; parallel-plate 15% only in 2002), and the optical response of real plates (Lifshitz 1956 supplied the framework). Having them does NOT change his conclusion inside its hypotheses: the ideal-plate coefficient is re-derived exactly here and the 2002 parallel-plate coefficient agrees at -0.45 sigma; the Drude/plasma 'Casimir puzzle' (2104.01460) is a dispute about real-material corrections of a few percent, not about the ideal limit. What the later data DO change is the domain: the ideal formula is the a >> lambda_p limit, and the tree evaluates it at 10 nm, 1 nm, 0.1 nm and 0.37 l_P, where the plasma-model interaction energy is 11%, 1.3%, 0.13% of it and the midpoint local density is positive. So M's hypothesis holds in a specific, non-favourable form: the data Casimir lacked narrow where his formula applies; it is not wrong, and every correction found runs AGAINST the device (smaller |rho|, larger shortfall), never for it. The energy density itself remains unobserved (Sopova-Ford p.16), so 'MEASURED' for rho is a discrepancy of status word, not a refutation.
grade_evidence: The published result STANDS on its own hypotheses: E/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 d^3), F/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(240 d^4) and the Brown-Maclay density -pi^2 hbar c/(720 d^4) re-derived symbolically (script A-C), the tree's numbers reproduce (D), no datum has moved (E), and the only parallel-plate measurement read agrees (pull -0.45 sigma). The TREE'S USE is on a larger class than the result covers: (1) it drops the perfect-conductor validity condition a >> lambda_p and evaluates the formula at 10 nm, 1 nm, 0.1 nm (achievable.py:124-141, 532-547; candidates.py:129-135) where plasma-model Lifshitz gives 0.111, 0.0130, 0.00132 of the ideal interaction energy (F); (2) it labels the energy density 'MEASURED' (achievable.py:31, 417-419; candidates.py:73-74) when only the force is measured, at 0.5-3 um parallel / >~120 nm sphere-plate; (3) its KIND pass (candidates.py:78) holds for a >~ 1.3 um (Al) but at its priced gaps the plasma-model midpoint density is positive (G). Not WRONG: no counterexample to the result as published. Direction: every narrowing reduces the available |rho|, so the tree's refusals (Casimir fails MAGNITUDE; corridors of light-years; crossover sub-Planckian) are unchanged or strengthened -- the numbers are ideal-plate upper bounds, not physical Casimir values.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owners restrict the use to ideal plates, relabel the density as the ideal-plate QFT value (force MEASURED, density inferred), and present the 10 nm / 0.1 nm / 1 nm rows as ideal-plate upper bounds. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a material model or measurement showing |rho| at nm gaps EXCEEDS the ideal value (none found; every model read gives less). To WRONG: a computed contradiction of the ideal-plate coefficient -- the symbolic re-derivation here rules that out. To OPEN: none; all load-bearing pieces were readable and checkable.
